brief.headline: Memory names whipsawed: Record H1 earnings clash with pricing-peak fears, hyperscaler capex still $725B, CoWoS gap tightening
brief.summary: Samsung and SK Hynix both posted record H1 2026 operating profit—Samsung ₩146T, Hynix ₩98T—but shares fell 6-9% today on post-earnings skepticism tracking WDC/SNDK misses overnight. Combined net cash set to hit $263B by year-end, triple Nvidia's. HBM3E remains mainstream (67% of 2026 HBM mix), HBM4 mass production now live at SK Hynix. DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in Q3, NAND +10-15%, decelerating but still tight. Big-5 hyperscaler capex confirmed at $725B for 2026, up 77% YoY. TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by year-end as monthly capacity hits 115-140k wafers.
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs Samsung. Hynix delivered 76% Q2 operating margin, 2x Samsung's profit, secured world's first HBM4 mass production system, holds >50% HBM market share through 2026 per Goldman, and is sole HBM3E supplier for Google TPU v7. Samsung still wrestling Nvidia HBM qualification, remains HBM3-heavy. Hynix M15X fab (₩20T investment) pilot ops begin May, targets both HBM3E/4. Relative valuation gap justified by 18-24 month technology lead. Near-term volatility high but structural edge intact.

memory_cycle.notes: Q1 2026 saw historic +93-98% QoQ DRAM contract price spike; Q2 +58-63%, Q3 tracking +13-18%—still double-digit but buyers hitting affordability ceiling. DDR4 8Gb spot at $24 in July, up 14.3% MoM, 8x since June 2016 trough. Supply structurally constrained as HBM/DDR5 server cannibalize legacy capacity. TrendForce flags 'shortage doesn't disappear' but pricing power moderating. HBM pricing diverging upward (20% 2026 hike reported), conventional DRAM entering mid-cycle repricing. NAND +70-75% in Q2, now +10-15% Q3 as eSSD enterprise demand (AI inference) offsets consumer weakness. Peak pricing likely H2 2026, correction risk rising into 2027 per multiple sell-side notes.

brief.hbm_pulse: HBM3E dominant through 2026 (TrendForce: 67% mix), HBM4 transition underway. SK Hynix secured first HBM4 mass production capacity Sept 2025, began shipments Q2 2026. Micron also in HBM4 high-volume production (36GB 12H). Samsung HBM4 targeting H1 2026 ramp but still qualifying 8-layer HBM3E with Nvidia—12-layer limited until Q2 2025 per prior reports. JEDEC HBM4 spec released April 2025: 2,048-bit interface, 2TB/s per stack, 32 channels. Nvidia Rubin and AMD MI455X are HBM4 pull-in platforms. China acquiring TC bonders for HBM3E 12-high stacks (export control workaround). Pricing: HBM3E reportedly +20% for 2026 contracts, HBM4 commanding 'significant premium' over HBM3 per industry sources. Supply remains Nvidia/Broadcom-captive; non-Big Tech customers facing allocation constraints.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix shares fall 6-9% today tracking WDC/SNDK overnight miss despite record H1 earnings
news_pulse.implication: Sentiment fragility: WDC's modest revenue guide triggered sector-wide repricing despite Samsung ₩146T/Hynix ₩98T H1 operating profit. Valuation compression risk if hyperscaler demand signals soften.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix to disclose expanded shareholder return plans by year-end; combined $263B net cash
news_pulse.implication: Cash generation exceeds Mag-7 ex-AAPL. Both targeting 50% FCF payout. Samsung ₩200T FCF estimate 2026, Hynix mid-₩100Ts. Buyback/dividend acceleration could narrow discount to US comps if sustained.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 8Gb spot hits $24 in July, +14.3% MoM; NAND $30.1, up 19 consecutive months
news_pulse.implication: Spot pricing still climbing but decelerating. Contract pricing guide: Q3 DRAM +13-18%, NAND +10-15% per TrendForce. Consumer resistance building; PC/smartphone OEMs balking at further increases.

news_pulse.headline: Big-5 hyperscaler 2026 capex confirmed at $725B, up 77% YoY; 75% directed to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $185B, Meta $125B, MSFT $120B. Oracle CDS spread widening on debt-funded buildout but aggregate demand signal intact. Memory capex subset drives HBM/DDR5 RDIMM/eSSD demand through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; capacity 115-140k wpm
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing as TSMC executes 80% CAGR 2022-27 expansion. 2027 capacity ~170k wpm. Nvidia 60% allocation intact, AMD/Broadcom spillover to Amkor/ASE. HBM attach constraint loosening into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q2 2026 revenue ₩79.3T (+257% YoY), 76% operating margin; stock fell 9% post-earnings
news_pulse.implication: Record financials met with profit-taking on pricing-peak concerns. M15X fab pilot ops May 2026, HBM4 mass production Q2 2026. Rubin platform pull-in supports H2 volume but Q3 guidance will be key tell.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Memory shortage extends to 2027, pricing deceleration not easing—buyer resistance rising
news_pulse.implication: Structural supply-demand imbalance persists (HBM capacity reallocation effect) but pricing power plateauing as consumer/enterprise customers resist sequential increases. Server segment remains healthy.

news_pulse.headline: HBM3E remains 67% of 2026 HBM mix; HBM4 transition led by SK Hynix, Micron in volume production
news_pulse.implication: Samsung HBM4 delayed vs peers; Nvidia Rubin/AMD MI455X HBM4 design wins at risk if qual doesn't close by Q4. Hynix/Micron dual-sourcing positions strengthen. HBM4E (1c DRAM) roadmap emerging 2027.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely range-bound near-term absent fresh catalyst. Elevated vol post-July drawdown (Samsung -37%, Hynix -48% from June peaks) suggests hedging demand persistent. Put skew elevated on memory names; consider selling near-term downside puts (5-10% OTM) into earnings volatility fade if hyperscaler capex commentary remains constructive. Watch USD/KRW—won strength headwind to export earnings but contained within ₩1,300-1,350 band YTD.
watch_for_next_3h: Any WDC/SNDK conference call transcript detail on enterprise SSD pricing or hyperscaler order pushouts—would validate/refute today's sell-off
TSMC August revenue release (due ~Aug 10)—CoWoS utilization proxy, especially CoWoS-L for Nvidia Rubin
Samsung/SK Hynix ADR price action in US premarket—institutional rotation signal if diverges from KRX close
Chinese CXMT HBM capability rumors—$8.6B IPO overhang noted in prior sell-off, any qual progress at domestic hyperscalers is margin risk
